sanskrit: nāsti kiṃ cit paraṃ bhūtaṃ mahādevād viśāṃ pate iha triṣv api lokeṣu bhūtānāṃ prabhavo hi saḥ
english: There is no being higher than Mahādeva, O lord of peoples; for here in all three worlds he is the source from which all beings arise.

sanskrit: na caivotsahate sthātuṃ kaś cid agre mahātmanaḥ na hi bhūtaṃ samaṃ tena triṣu lokeṣu vidyate
english: No one dares to stand before that great-souled one, for no being equal to him is found in the three worlds.

sanskrit: gandhenāpi hi saṃgrāme tasya kruddhasya śatravaḥ visaṃjñā hatabhūyiṣṭhā vepanti ca patanti ca
english: In battle, by his very scent when he is enraged, his enemies lose their senses, are all but slain, tremble, and fall.

sanskrit: ghoraṃ ca ninadaṃ tasya parjanyaninadopamam śrutvā vidīryed dhṛdayaṃ devānām api saṃyuge
english: Hearing his terrible roar, like the thundercloud's thunder, in battle the very heart of the gods would burst asunder.

sanskrit: yāṃś ca ghoreṇa rūpeṇa paśyet kruddhaḥ pinākadhṛk na surā nāsurā loke na gandharvā na pannagāḥ kupite sukham edhante tasminn api guhāgatāḥ
english: Those whom the wielder of the Pināka, enraged, looks upon with his terrible form—neither gods nor demons in this world, neither gandharvas nor serpents thrive in ease when he is wrathful, even if they have fled into a cave.

sanskrit: prajāpateś ca dakṣasya yajato vitate kratau vivyādha kupito yajñaṃ nirbhayas tu bhavas tadā dhanuṣā bāṇam utsṛjya saghoṣaṃ vinanāda ca
english: When the Prajāpati Dakṣa was performing his far-extended sacrifice, Bhava, enraged and fearless, pierced the sacrifice through; releasing an arrow from his bow, he roared aloud with a great cry.

sanskrit: te na śarma kutaḥ śāntiṃ viṣādaṃ lebhire surāḥ vidrute sahasā yajñe kupite ca maheśvare
english: The gods found no refuge—how then peace?—but only despair, when the sacrifice was suddenly scattered and Maheśvara was enraged.

sanskrit: tena jyātalaghoṣeṇa sarve lokāḥ samākulāḥ babhūvur avaśāḥ pārtha viṣeduś ca surāsurāḥ
english: By that twang of the bowstring against the wristguard all the worlds were thrown into turmoil and grew helpless, O Pārtha, and gods and demons alike sank in despair.

sanskrit: āpaś cukṣubhire caiva cakampe ca vasuṃdharā vyadravan girayaś cāpi dyauḥ paphāla ca sarvaśaḥ
english: The waters were churned up, the earth quaked, the mountains ran loose, and the heavens split apart on every side.

sanskrit: andhena tamasā lokāḥ prāvṛtā na cakāśire pranaṣṭā jyotiṣāṃ bhāś ca saha sūryeṇa bhārata
english: Shrouded in blinding darkness, the worlds shone no longer, and the radiance of the luminaries, along with the sun, was lost, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ bhītās tataḥ śāntiṃ cakruḥ svastyayanāni ca ṛṣayaḥ sarvabhūtānām ātmanaś ca hitaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Then, sorely afraid, the sages, seeking the welfare of all beings and of themselves, performed rites of appeasement and benediction.

sanskrit: tataḥ so 'bhyadravad devān kruddho raudraparākramaḥ bhagasya nayane kruddhaḥ prahāreṇa vyaśātayat
english: Then he, of terrible prowess, in his fury rushed upon the gods, and in his wrath struck out Bhaga's eyes with a single blow.

sanskrit: pūṣāṇaṃ cābhidudrāva pareṇa vapuṣānvitaḥ puroḍāśaṃ bhakṣayato daśanān vai vyaśātayat
english: Endowed with a transcendent form, he charged upon Pūṣan, and as he was eating the sacrificial cake he knocked out his teeth.

sanskrit: tataḥ praṇemur devās te vepamānāḥ sma śaṃkaram punaś ca saṃdadhe rudro dīptaṃ suniśitaṃ śaram
english: Then those gods, trembling, bowed down to Śaṃkara; yet Rudra fitted again to his bow a blazing, keen-edged arrow.

sanskrit: rudrasya vikramaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhītā devāḥ saharṣibhiḥ tataḥ prasādayām āsuḥ śarvaṃ te vibudhottamāḥ
english: Beholding Rudra's might, the gods together with the sages grew afraid; then those foremost of the wise sought to propitiate Śarva.

sanskrit: jepuś ca śatarudrīyaṃ devāḥ kṛtvāñjaliṃ tataḥ saṃstūyamānas tridaśaiḥ prasasāda maheśvaraḥ
english: With folded hands the gods then murmured the Śatarudrīya, and, praised by the thirty, Maheśvara was appeased.

sanskrit: rudrasya bhāgaṃ yajñe ca viśiṣṭaṃ te tv akalpayan bhayena tridaśā rājañ śaraṇaṃ ca prapedire
english: They assigned to Rudra a special share in the sacrifice, and in their fear, O king, the thirty took refuge in him.

sanskrit: tena caivātikopena sa yajñaḥ saṃdhito 'bhavat yad yac cāpi hataṃ tatra tat tathaiva pradīyate
english: Through that very excess of his wrath the sacrifice was made whole again, and whatever had been destroyed there was restored just as it had been.

sanskrit: asurāṇāṃ purāṇy āsaṃs trīṇi vīryavatāṃ divi āyasaṃ rājataṃ caiva sauvarṇam aparaṃ tathā
english: The mighty asuras had three cities in the sky: one of iron, one of silver, and yet another of gold.

sanskrit: nāśakat tāni maghavā bhettuṃ sarvāyudhair api atha sarve 'marā rudraṃ jagmuḥ śaraṇamarditāḥ
english: Maghavan could not breach them even with all his weapons; then all the immortals, sore beset, went to Rudra for refuge.

sanskrit: tata ūcur mahātmāno devāḥ sarve samāgatāḥ rudra raudrā bhaviṣyanti paśavaḥ sarvakarmasu jahi daityān saha purair lokāṃs trāyasva mānada
english: Then all the great-souled gods, assembled together, spoke: 'Rudra, in every rite the sacrificial victims shall be yours; slay the daityas together with their cities and save the worlds, O giver of honor!'

sanskrit: sa tathoktas tathety uktvā viṣṇuṃ kṛtvā śarottamam śalyam agniṃ tathā kṛtvā puṅkhaṃ vaivasvataṃ yamam vedān kṛtvā dhanuḥ sarvāñ jyāṃ ca sāvitrim uttamām
english: Thus addressed, he answered 'So be it,' and making Viṣṇu his choicest shaft, Agni its barb, and Yama son of Vivasvat its feathered tip, making all the Vedas his bow and the supreme Sāvitrī its string,

sanskrit: devān rathavaraṃ kṛtvā viniyujya ca sarvaśaḥ triparvaṇā triśalyena tena tāni bibheda saḥ
english: and making the gods his excellent chariot, and yoking them all together, with that three-jointed, three-barbed arrow he pierced those cities through.

sanskrit: śareṇādityavarṇena kālāgnisamatejasā te 'surāḥ sapurās tatra dagdhā rudreṇa bhārata
english: By that arrow, sun-colored and blazing like the fire of doom, those asuras together with their cities were burned up there by Rudra, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: taṃ caivāṅkagataṃ dṛṣṭvā bālaṃ pañcaśikhaṃ punaḥ umā jijñāsamānā vai ko 'yam ity abravīt tadā
english: And when she saw him seated on her lap as a child with five locks of hair, Umā, wishing to know, then asked, 'Who is this?'

sanskrit: asūyataś ca śakrasya vajreṇa prahariṣyataḥ savajraṃ stambhayām āsa taṃ bāhuṃ parighopamam
english: And when Śakra, resentful, made ready to strike with his thunderbolt, he froze fast that arm, club-like, together with its thunderbolt.

sanskrit: na saṃbubudhire cainaṃ devās taṃ bhuvaneśvaram saprajāpatayaḥ sarve tasmin mumuhur īśvare
english: The gods did not recognize him, that lord of the worlds; all of them, together with the Prajāpatis, were bewildered before that Lord.

sanskrit: tato dhyātvātha bhagavān brahmā tam amitaujasam ayaṃ śreṣṭha iti jñātvā vavande tam umāpatim
english: Then the lord Brahmā, meditating, knew that one of boundless energy: realizing 'This is the supreme one,' he bowed down to that consort of Umā.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasādayām āsur umāṃ rudraṃ ca te surāḥ babhūva sa tadā bāhur balahantur yathā purā
english: Then those gods propitiated Umā and Rudra, and the arm of the slayer of Bala became then as it was before.

sanskrit: sa cāpi brāhmaṇo bhūtvā durvāsā nāma vīryavān dvāravatyāṃ mama gṛhe ciraṃ kālam upāvasat
english: And that same one, becoming a brāhmaṇa, the mighty Durvāsas by name, dwelt for a long while in my house at Dvāravatī.

sanskrit: viprakārān prayuṅkte sma subahūn mama veśmani tān udāratayā cāham akṣamaṃ tasya duḥsaham
english: He inflicted many vexations within my dwelling, and out of magnanimity I bore patiently with him things hard to bear and beyond his deserving.

sanskrit: sa devendraś ca vāyuś ca so 'śvinau sa ca vidyutaḥ sa candramāḥ sa ceśānaḥ sa sūryo varuṇaś ca saḥ
english: He is Indra lord of gods, and Vāyu; he is the two Aśvins, and he is the lightnings; he is the moon, he is Īśāna, he is the sun and Varuṇa.

sanskrit: sa kālaḥ so 'ntako mṛtyuḥ sa tamo rātryahāni ca māsārdhamāsā ṛtavaḥ saṃdhye saṃvatsaraś ca saḥ
english: He is Time, he is the Ender, Death; he is darkness, the nights and the days, the months and the half-months, the seasons, the twilights, and the year.

sanskrit: sa dhātā sa vidhātā ca viśvakarmā sa sarvavit nakṣatrāṇi diśaś caiva pradiśo 'tha grahās tathā viśvamūrtir ameyātmā bhagavān amitadyutiḥ
english: He is Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, he is Viśvakarman the all-knowing; the constellations, the quarters and intermediate quarters, and likewise the planets—he, whose form is the universe, whose self is immeasurable, the lord of boundless splendor.

sanskrit: ekadhā ca dvidhā caiva bahudhā ca sa eva ca śatadhā sahasradhā caiva tathā śatasahasradhā
english: He is onefold, and twofold, and manifold; he becomes a hundredfold, and a thousandfold, and likewise a hundred-thousandfold.

sanskrit: īdṛśaḥ sa mahādevo bhūyaś ca bhagavān ataḥ na hi śakyā guṇā vaktum api varṣaśatair api
english: Such is that Mahādeva, and the lord is yet more than this; for his virtues cannot be told even in a hundred years.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho mahābhāgyaṃ mahātmanaḥ rudrāya bahurūpāya bahunāmne nibodha me
english: Vāsudeva said: O mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, learn from me the great glory of the great-souled one, of Rudra of many forms and many names.

sanskrit: vadanty agniṃ mahādevaṃ tathā sthāṇuṃ maheśvaram ekākṣaṃ tryambakaṃ caiva viśvarūpaṃ śivaṃ tathā
english: They call him Agni, Mahādeva, and Sthāṇu, Maheśvara, the One-Eyed, the Three-Eyed, and the All-Formed, and Śiva.

sanskrit: dve tanū tasya devasya vedajñā brāhmaṇā viduḥ ghorām anyāṃ śivām anyāṃ te tanū bahudhā punaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇas learned in the Veda know that god to have two bodies—the one terrible, the other benign; and these two bodies are again of many kinds.

sanskrit: ugrā ghorā tanūr yāsya so 'gnir vidyut sa bhāskaraḥ śivā saumyā ca yā tasya dharmas tv āpo 'tha candramāḥ
english: His fierce and terrible body is Agni, the lightning, the sun; while his benign and gentle one is Dharma, the waters, and the moon.

sanskrit: ātmano 'rdhaṃ tu tasyāgnir ucyate bharatarṣabha brahmacaryaṃ caraty eṣa śivā yāsya tanus tathā
english: Half of his self is said to be Agni, O bull of the Bhāratas; and that benign body of his practices chastity.

sanskrit: yāsya ghoratamā mūrtir jagat saṃharate tayā īśvaratvān mahattvāc ca maheśvara iti smṛtaḥ
english: His most terrible form, by which he dissolves the world—because of his lordship and his greatness he is therefore remembered as Maheśvara, the Great Lord.

sanskrit: yan nirdahati yat tīkṣṇo yad ugro yat pratāpavān māṃsaśoṇitamajjādo yat tato rudra ucyate
english: Because he burns wholly, because he is fierce, because he is dreadful, because he is full of fiery power, and because he devours flesh, blood, and marrow—therefore he is called Rudra.

sanskrit: devānāṃ sumahān yac ca yac cāsya viṣayo mahān yac ca viśvaṃ mahat pāti mahādevas tataḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Because he is the greatest of the gods, because his domain is great, and because he guards the whole great universe, he is therefore remembered as Mahādeva, the Great God.

sanskrit: samedhayati yan nityaṃ sarvārthān sarvakarmabhiḥ śivam icchan manuṣyāṇāṃ tasmād eṣa śivaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Because he ever prospers all aims through all rites, desiring the welfare of men, he is therefore remembered as Śiva, the Auspicious.

sanskrit: dahaty ūrdhvaṃ sthito yac ca prāṇotpattiḥ sthitiś ca yat sthiraliṅgaś ca yan nityaṃ tasmāt sthāṇur iti smṛtaḥ
english: Because, standing erect, he burns, because he is the origin and continuance of life, and because his emblem stands ever firm, he is therefore remembered as Sthāṇu, the Steadfast.

sanskrit: yad asya bahudhā rūpaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhavat tathā sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva bahurūpas tataḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Because his form is manifold—the past, the future, and the present, the unmoving and the moving alike—he is therefore remembered as Bahurūpa, the One of Many Forms.

sanskrit: dhūmraṃ rūpaṃ ca yat tasya dhūrjaṭīty ata ucyate viśve devāś ca yat tasmin viśvarūpas tataḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Because his form is smoke-gray, he is therefore called Dhūrjaṭi, the Smoke-Matted; and because the All-Gods are within him, he is therefore remembered as Viśvarūpa, the All-Formed.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣo 'yutākṣo vā sarvatokṣimayo 'pi vā cakṣuṣaḥ prabhavas tejo nāsty anto 'thāsya cakṣuṣām
english: Thousand-eyed, or ten-thousand-eyed, or made of eyes on every side—he is the source of sight, the radiance of vision, and there is no end to his eyes.

sanskrit: sarvathā yat paśūn pāti taiś ca yad ramate punaḥ teṣām adhipatir yac ca tasmāt paśupatiḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Because in every way he protects the creatures, and again because he sports with them, and because he is their overlord, he is therefore remembered as Paśupati, Lord of Creatures.

sanskrit: nityena brahmacaryeṇa liṅgam asya yadā sthitam mahayanty asya lokāś ca maheśvara iti smṛtaḥ
english: Because his emblem stands firm through perpetual chastity, and because the worlds magnify him, he is therefore remembered as Maheśvara, the Great Lord.

sanskrit: vigrahaṃ pūjayed yo vai liṅgaṃ vāpi mahātmanaḥ liṅgaṃ pūjayitā nityaṃ mahatīṃ śriyam aśnute
english: Whoever worships the image of that great-souled one, or his emblem—he who ever worships the emblem attains to great prosperity.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś cāpi devāś ca gandharvāpsarasas tathā liṅgam evārcayanti sma yat tad ūrdhvaṃ samāsthitam
english: And the sages too, and the gods, and the gandharvas and apsarases, worship that very emblem which stands erect on high.

sanskrit: pūjyamāne tatas tasmin modate sa maheśvaraḥ sukhaṃ dadāti prītātmā bhaktānāṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ
english: When it is being worshipped, Maheśvara rejoices, and with gladdened heart he grants happiness to his devotees, he who cherishes those who love him.

sanskrit: eṣa eva śmaśāneṣu devo vasati nityaśaḥ yajante taṃ janās tatra vīrasthānaniṣeviṇam
english: This same god dwells perpetually in the cremation grounds, and there men worship him, the haunter of heroes' places.

sanskrit: viṣamasthaḥ śarīreṣu sa mṛtyuḥ prāṇinām iha sa ca vāyuḥ śarīreṣu prāṇo 'pānaḥ śarīriṇām
english: Lodged in the body's disorders, he is the death of living creatures here; and he is the breath within bodies, the prāṇa and apāna of the embodied.

sanskrit: tasya ghorāṇi rūpāṇi dīptāni ca bahūni ca loke yāny asya pūjyante viprās tāni vidur budhāḥ
english: His many forms, terrible and blazing, which are worshipped in the world—the wise brāhmaṇas know them.

sanskrit: nāmadheyāni vedeṣu bahūny asya yathārthataḥ nirucyante mahattvāc ca vibhutvāt karmabhis tathā
english: His many names in the Vedas are derived according to their meaning—from his greatness, his all-pervading power, and his deeds.

sanskrit: vede cāsya vidur viprāḥ śatarudrīyam uttamam vyāsād anantaraṃ yac cāpy upasthānaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: And in the Veda the brāhmaṇas know his supreme Śatarudrīya, and the worship of that great-souled one that follows immediately upon the dispersion.

sanskrit: pradātā sarvalokānāṃ viśvaṃ cāpy ucyate mahat jyeṣṭhabhūtaṃ vadanty enaṃ brāhmaṇā ṛṣayo 'pare
english: He is the bestower upon all the worlds, and he is called the great universe; the brāhmaṇas and other sages declare him to be the eldest-born of beings.

sanskrit: prathamo hy eṣa devānāṃ mukhād agnir ajāyata grahair bahuvidhaiḥ prāṇān saṃruddhān utsṛjaty api
english: For he is the first of the gods; Agni was born from his mouth; and though life-breaths are held fast by manifold seizures, he sets them free.

sanskrit: sa mocayati puṇyātmā śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatān āyur ārogyam aiśvaryaṃ vittaṃ kāmāṃś ca puṣkalān
english: That holy-souled one, the giver of refuge, delivers those who come to him for refuge, granting them long life, health, lordship, wealth, and abundant desires.

sanskrit: sa dadāti manuṣyebhyaḥ sa evākṣipate punaḥ śakrādiṣu ca deveṣu tasya caiśvaryam ucyate
english: These he gives to men, and these again he takes away; and his lordship is declared to abide in Śakra and the other gods.

sanskrit: sa evābhyadhiko nityaṃ trailokyasya śubhāśubhe aiśvaryāc caiva kāmānām īśvaraḥ punar ucyate
english: He alone is ever supreme in the weal and woe of the three worlds; and because he is sovereign over all desires, he is again called Īśvara, the Lord.

sanskrit: maheśvaraś ca lokānāṃ mahatām īśvaraś ca saḥ bahubhir vividhai rūpair viśvaṃ vyāptam idaṃ jagat tasya devasya yad vaktraṃ samudre vaḍavāmukham
english: He is Maheśvara, the great lord of the worlds, and the lord of the mighty ones; by his many and various forms this whole universe is pervaded; and the mouth of that god is the mare's-mouth fire within the ocean.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktavati vākyaṃ tu kṛṣṇe devakinandane bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ bhūyaḥ paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, had spoken this discourse, Yudhiṣṭhira once more questioned Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: nirṇaye vā mahābuddhe sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ vara pratyakṣam āgamo veti kiṃ tayoḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavet
english: O greatly wise one, foremost of all upholders of dharma, in reaching a certain conclusion, which of the two—direct perception or scriptural tradition—should be the authority?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ kaś cid iti me vartate matiḥ śṛṇu vakṣyāmi te prājña samyak tvam anupṛcchasi
english: Bhīṣma said: My judgment holds that there is no doubt at all in this matter. Listen, O wise one; I shall tell you, for you ask rightly.

sanskrit: saṃśayaḥ sugamo rājan nirṇayas tv atra durgamaḥ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutam anantaṃ hi yatra saṃśayadarśanam
english: Doubt is easy to reach, O king, but certainty here is hard to attain; for where doubt appears, the seen and the heard are without end.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ kāraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ hetukāḥ prājñamāninaḥ nāstīty evaṃ vyavasyanti satyaṃ saṃśayam eva ca tad ayuktaṃ vyavasyanti bālāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ
english: The reasoners, who fancy themselves wise, hold direct perception to be the seen authority and conclude 'it does not exist,' thus turning truth itself into mere doubt; childish men who deem themselves learned conclude what is unfitting.

sanskrit: atha cen manyase caikaṃ kāraṇaṃ kiṃ bhaved iti śakyaṃ dīrgheṇa kālena yuktenātandritena ca prāṇayātrām anekāṃ ca kalpayānena bhārata
english: But if you ask which one might be the true authority, that can be reached, O Bhārata, only over a long time, by one who is disciplined and untiring and who has provided for the sustenance of many lives.

sanskrit: tatpareṇaiva nānyena śakyaṃ hy etat tu kāraṇam hetūnām antam āsādya vipulaṃ jñānam uttamam jyotiḥ sarvasya lokasya vipulaṃ pratipadyate
english: This authority can be grasped only by one wholly devoted to it and by no other; reaching the limit of all causes, he attains vast and supreme knowledge, the boundless light of all the world.

sanskrit: tattvenāgamanaṃ rājan hetvantagamanaṃ tathā agrāhyam anibaddhaṃ ca vācaḥ saṃparivarjanam
english: Arriving at the truth, O king, and so reaching the end of causes, one must shun all speech that is ungraspable and unfounded.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pratyakṣaṃ lokataḥ siddhaṃ lokāś cāgamapūrvakāḥ śiṣṭācāro bahuvidho brūhi tan me pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Direct perception is established from the world, and the worlds rest upon scriptural tradition; the conduct of the cultivated is of many kinds—explain this to me, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca dharmasya hriyamāṇasya balavadbhir durātmabhiḥ saṃsthā yatnair api kṛtā kālena paribhidyate
english: Bhīṣma said: When dharma is being carried off by the powerful and the wicked, even the order established by great efforts is broken down by time.

sanskrit: adharmā dharmarūpeṇa tṛṇaiḥ kūpā ivāvṛtāḥ tatas tair bhidyate vṛttaṃ śṛṇu caiva yudhiṣṭhira
english: Unrighteous deeds, wearing the guise of dharma, are like wells hidden over with grass; by these, right conduct is broken—hear this, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: avṛttyā ye ca bhindanti śrutatyāgaparāyaṇāḥ dharmavidveṣiṇo mandā ity uktas teṣu saṃśayaḥ
english: Those who, by their misconduct, break down right conduct—who are bent on abandoning the sacred lore, who hate dharma, and who are dull-witted—about such men doubt has been declared to arise.

sanskrit: atṛpyantas tu sādhūnāṃ ya evāgamabuddhayaḥ param ity eva saṃtuṣṭās tān upāssva ca pṛccha ca
english: But those whose minds rest upon scripture, who are never sated of the company of the good, and who are content saying 'This is supreme'—wait upon such men and question them.

sanskrit: kāmārthau pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā lobhamohānusāriṇau dharma ity eva saṃbuddhās tān upāssva ca pṛccha ca
english: Those who, casting behind them desire and gain—which follow upon greed and delusion—are awakened to dharma alone: wait upon such men and question them.

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ bhidyate vṛttaṃ yajñasvādhyāyakarmabhiḥ ācāraḥ kāraṇaṃ caiva dharmaś caiva trayaṃ punaḥ
english: Their conduct is never broken by the rites of sacrifice and Vedic study; and these three again—right practice, scriptural authority, and dharma—stand firm.
